defs.message: trap arm pattern must be a predicate `.{ .field <op> value, ... }`
defs.note: trap arm predicate must be `.{ .field <op> value, ... }`

defs.name: TRAP_RESUME_FORM
defs.note: `resume(...)` argument must be a `.repair-name` (use `.abort` to propagate)

defs.name: TRAP_ARM_BODY
defs.message: trap arm body must be `resume(.name)` or `recover(<expr>)`
defs.note: trap arm body must be `resume(.name)` or `recover(<expr>)`

defs.name: TRAP_POSITION
defs.message: `trap` is only allowed in `return trap ...;` and `var x: T = trap ...;`
defs.note: `trap` is only allowed in `return trap ...;` and `var x: T = trap ...;`

defs.name: TRAP_NOT_FAULT
defs.note: trap scrutinee must have type `fault(E)!T`

defs.name: TRAP_PRED_MEMBER
defs.message: trap arm predicate does not match any member of the fault group
defs.note: trap arm predicate does not match any member of the fault group

defs.name: TRAP_DUP_MEMBER
defs.message: trap arm covers a fault member already handled by an earlier arm
defs.note: two trap arms land on the same fault member (the latter never fires)

defs.name: TRAP_ABORT_POSITION
defs.note: `.abort` requires `return trap ...;` in a function whose signature carries `fault(E)!T`

defs.name: TRAP_NONEXHAUSTIVE
defs.message: `trap` without `.abort` must cover every member of the fault group
defs.note: a trap without an `.abort` arm must cover every member of the fault group

defs.name: TRAP_REPAIR_SLOT
defs.message: repair name is not declared for the fault member of this trap arm
defs.note: trap arm repair name is not declared for that fault member

defs.name: TRAP_WILD_ONLY_ABORT
defs.message: the wildcard trap arm `_` accepts only `resume(.abort)`
defs.note: the wildcard trap arm `_` only accepts `resume(.abort)`

defs.name: FAULT_ESCAPE_PUB_NEEDS_DECL
defs.message: pub function can raise `<E>`; it must declare `fault(E)!T` explicitly
defs.note: a `pub fn` must explicitly declare `fault(E)!T` (non-pub fns may omit it; v1 inference supports a single group)

defs.name: FAULT_ESCAPE_MULTI_GROUP
defs.message: function escapes faults of more than one group; v1 derivation supports a single group
defs.note: function escapes faults of more than one group; v1 supports a single group
